Domain.Name: GRACE Workflow Runtime
Domain.Description: Product-local redesign of GRACE around a deterministic workflow state machine, explicit transitions, machine-enforced guards, and bounded agent execution windows.

Actor.Name: Workflow Owner
Actor.Description: Human operator who initiates delivery, approves handoffs, and resolves escalations.

Actor.Name: Coordinator Runtime
Actor.Description: State-machine orchestrator that routes transitions and enforces policy guards.

Actor.Name: Bounded Agent Executor
Actor.Description: Architect, coordinator, or coder executor running only inside a permitted transition window.

UseCase.Name: Persist and advance the workflow state machine
UseCase.Description: Maintain one canonical workflow state per product and move it only through approved transitions.

AAG.Action: loads state, evaluates one requested transition, and persists the resulting state and transition event
AAG.Goal: prevent undocumented or illegal process movement

Preconditions.Item: A product-local workflow state document exists or can be initialized deterministically.
The requested transition name and actor identity are explicit.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Every process movement is recorded as a validated transition from one named state to another.

UseCase.Name: Enforce transition guards and actor permissions
UseCase.Description: Prevent agents or humans from performing transitions without the required artifacts, approvals, scope, and role permissions.

AAG.Action: evaluates policy guards before permitting a transition
AAG.Goal: make GRACE governance machine-enforced instead of prompt-enforced

Preconditions.Item: Policy documents defining actor permissions and transition guards are present.
Artifact references for the attempted transition are resolvable.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Illegal transitions are rejected deterministically with an issue report or blocked state.

UseCase.Name: Handle approval interrupts inside the workflow
UseCase.Description: Pause at approval boundaries and resume only after a human approval event is formally recorded.

AAG.Action: approves or rejects a pending handoff or escalation
AAG.Goal: retain explicit human control at critical governance checkpoints

Preconditions.Item: The workflow is in an approval-pending state.
The relevant handoff or escalation artifact has been materialized.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: The workflow either advances to an approved state or is blocked/rejected with a durable decision record.

UseCase.Name: Run architect, coordinator, and coder as bounded executors
UseCase.Description: Invoke agent roles only within the semantic and temporal scope granted by the active transition.

AAG.Goal: produce artifacts or code without process authority leakage

Preconditions.Item: An active transition grants scope to the role and names allowed artifacts or semantic ids.
The workflow is not blocked.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Role execution is traceable, policy-bounded, and cannot illegally change global process state.

UseCase.Name: Preserve workflow-to-artifact traceability
UseCase.Description: Keep one stable delivery trace across workflow state, transitions, handoffs, CWOs, execution artifacts, skill traces, and verification outputs.

AAG.Action: binds every transition and effect to the active delivery trace
AAG.Goal: make the process auditable end to end

Preconditions.Item: A stable trace id exists for the delivery stream.
Execution artifacts and reports are written through transition effects.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Auditors can reconstruct the full chain from transition log to runtime evidence and approvals.

UseCase.Name: Route repeated failures through forced-context remediation
UseCase.Description: Integrate the current W11 autonomy cycle as a governed branch of the main workflow state machine.

AAG.Action: captures failure artifacts, applies loop guards, and reopens remediation only when allowed

Preconditions.Item: Failure envelope, failure memory, and loop guard validators are available.
The workflow is in a verification or remediation failure state.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Repeated failures become explicit governed states rather than hidden retry loops.

UseCase.Name: Invoke legacy GRACE validators through governed adapters
UseCase.Description: Run mature v1 validation and trace scripts as bounded adapter effects under v2 workflow control instead of relying on direct ad hoc script orchestration.

AAG.Action: invokes legacy validator adapters as named workflow effects
AAG.Goal: reuse trusted v1 evidence tooling during migration without returning process control to script-first orchestration

Preconditions.Item: Compatible v1 scripts and their inputs are available in the repository.
The v2 workflow has already established one canonical state, trace id, and artifact chain.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Legacy validators produce evidence under v2 control and can be phased out later without breaking the product workflow model.

UseCase.Name: Onboard external legacy repositories into governed GRACE overlays
UseCase.Description: Create a GRACE-controlled overlay workspace for an existing repository so workflow state, policy, and traceability can be applied without rewriting the source tree up front.

AAG.Action: creates and advances a governed overlay over a legacy repository
AAG.Goal: bring unstructured code under deterministic workflow control

Preconditions.Item: A resolvable source repository root exists outside or alongside the overlay workspace.
The overlay workspace can materialize GRACE state, policy, and reports independently from the source repository.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: The legacy repository is addressable by state, trace, and bounded execution before any invasive code change begins.

UseCase.Name: Bootstrap a read-only overlay for legacy code
UseCase.Description: Materialize workflow, policy, and metadata artifacts for a legacy repository without modifying the underlying source code.

AAG.Action: bootstraps a GRACE overlay over an existing repository
AAG.Goal: prepare the repository for governed discovery and slicing

Preconditions.Item: The source repository root is reachable and readable.
The overlay workspace location is writable.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: A valid legacy overlay exists and can be validated independently from the source repository.

UseCase.Name: Protect legacy source repositories during onboarding
UseCase.Description: Keep legacy onboarding read-only until explicit approval and write-mode authorization allow bounded source edits.

AAG.Action: enforces write restrictions on the source repository
AAG.Goal: prevent accidental invasive changes during onboarding and early discovery

Preconditions.Item: The workflow can distinguish overlay workspace artifacts from source repository paths.
Policy files declare whether write mode is enabled.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Unauthorized writes to the source repository are blocked deterministically with durable evidence.

UseCase.Name: Expose legacy onboarding through MCP
UseCase.Description: Allow external MCP clients to bootstrap, scan, validate, and advance legacy onboarding through governed GRACE actions.

AAG.Action: uses MCP tools to onboard and inspect a legacy repository
AAG.Goal: operate GRACE on legacy code without manual file surgery

Preconditions.Item: The grace-mcp server is connected to the repository and can resolve both overlay and source roots.
The target repository has been declared or bootstrapped as a legacy overlay.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Legacy onboarding can be driven entirely through MCP while preserving workflow governance.

UseCase.Name: Scan and map legacy repository structure
UseCase.Description: Discover files, modules, languages, tests, entrypoints, and structural risks before contract inference or code changes begin.

AAG.Action: scans a legacy repository and emits structural reports
AAG.Goal: replace blind whole-repo reading with machine-readable discovery artifacts

Preconditions.Item: The overlay knows the source repository root.
The repository is readable.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: The system has a durable scan and risk baseline for the repository.

UseCase.Name: Infer draft contracts from legacy code
UseCase.Description: Generate draft module, function, and block contracts over existing code so legacy modification can become contract-guided.

AAG.Action: derives draft MC, FC, and BA anchors from legacy code
AAG.Goal: create a semantic shield before modification begins

Preconditions.Item: A structural scan and repository map already exist.
The workflow is in a legacy contract inference state.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: Legacy code gains draft semantic contracts and trace seeds without source mutation.

UseCase.Name: Propose the first safe legacy modification slices
UseCase.Description: Use scan, inferred contracts, and risk reports to propose bounded first changes suitable for governed coder execution.

AAG.Action: derives bounded first slices from the legacy graph and risks
AAG.Goal: avoid uncontrolled first edits in large legacy codebases

Preconditions.Item: Legacy scan and contract draft artifacts already exist.
Write mode is still disabled or limited to dry-run planning.

UseCase.SuccessOutcome: The workflow produces reviewable, bounded, FC-scoped first slices for safe legacy edits.

DataContract.Description: Canonical persisted workflow state for one product delivery stream.
Append-only event describing one legal or rejected state transition.
Machine-readable transition rules, actor permissions, and guard declarations.
Deterministic issue record emitted when a guard fails or the workflow enters a blocked state.
Overlay metadata describing the relationship between the GRACE workspace and the external legacy source repository.
Machine-readable discovery and risk report for a legacy repository.
Draft semantic contracts inferred from legacy source code without mutating the codebase.

NFR.Statement: Critical process transitions must be decided by machine-enforced guards and state transitions, not by prompt interpretation alone.
Every state transition must produce durable, reviewable evidence with actor identity, trace id, and artifact refs.
Architect, coordinator, and coder executors must not be able to modify workflow state outside their authorized transitions.
The workflow engine must resume safely after interruption using persisted state and transition history.
GRACE should reuse existing handoff, approval, CWO, execution-proof, delivery-trace, and autonomy artifacts as effects rather than replacing them immediately.
Legacy onboarding must default to a non-invasive overlay mode that does not modify the source repository before explicit authorization.
